newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes flat on high dlr supply.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes flat on high dlr supply.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed flat against the dollar on Friday, due to the market being well supplied with dollars, dealers said.
The rupee closed at its opening level of 58.85 to the dollar.
"The market is so well supplied with dollars, that a little bit of demand makes no impact at all," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by one local cent, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.8382 and 60.0268.
Overnight call money rates were steady at 8.875 prcent, again due to the market being well offered, dealers said.
The Central Bank overnight repo rate was at 8.5 percent.
Dealers say the dollar-rupee exchange rate should be stable in the short term due to easing inflation, steady interest rates and the privatisation programme being on track.
Sri Lanka said annual average inflation fell to 13.9 percent in July from 14.7 in June.
The government is expected to announce the sale of 35 percent and management in Sri Lanka Telecom and its holding of 27.5 million 10-rupee convertible debentures in the National DevelopmentBank Ltd.
"Both these transactions should see substantial net foreign inflows, which will have a calming effect on the exchange rate," said one.
